Youth scrabble outfit on their return to Sri Lanka

Sri Lanka’s youth Scrabble team delivered an outstanding performance on the world stage, securing third place overall at the World Youth Scrabble Championship (WYSC) 2026, which concluded in Kenya recently.

Represented by a strong contingent of 10 young players, Sri Lanka competed against some of the world’s best junior Scrabble minds during the prestigious international tournament.

The Sri Lankan challenge was spearheaded by Tharin Kariyawasam of Richmond College, Galle, who produced an impressive performance to finish eighth overall with 16 wins, earning a place among the world’s top 10 youth players. He was closely followed by Kevan Croos of S. Thomas’ College, Mount Lavinia, who finished 15th with 15 wins, while Pasindu Wijewardena of Stafford International School secured 20th place, also with 15 wins.

Combining these top-level finishes, the team recorded an impressive average rating of 14.33 to secure third place on the World Championship podium this year out of 22 outfits, which is a remarkable achievement.

While the performances of these three highest-ranked players anchored the team’s placement, the achievement was the result of the collective effort and competitive spirit demonstrated by the entire national squad throughout the gruelling event.

The following seven players also competed for the Sri Lankan national team: Aayush Haputhanthiri (Richmond College, Galle); Kyaan Perera and Omiru Nandasiri (S. Thomas’ College, Mount Lavinia); Inam Irshad and Imad Irshad (Gateway College, Colombo); Aathif Kamil Rishard (Royal College, Colombo); and Kaumadee Balasinghe (Girls’ High School, Kandy). (SJ)

title: Miraz looks ahead as Bangladesh eye Australia series triumph | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 18 August 2026 10:47
-     - 0

Bangladesh all-rounder Mehidy Hasan Miraz is eyeing off an historic series triumph in Australia as the Asian side look to boost their chances of appearing in next year’s ICC World Test Championship Final.

Miraz played a starring role in Bangladesh’s upset nine-wicket victory over the Aussies in Darwin in the first match of the two-game series, with the 28-year-old scoring a half-century to help give his side the ascendancy before completing a five-wicket haul on the final day to ensure the result.

It provides Bangladesh the opportunity to clinch a rare 2-0 series result when the teams move to Mackay in north Queensland for the second and final Test of the series and Miraz believes his side is well placed to complete the rout.

“Of course we are thinking that way (clinching the series) and we want to stay focused on the approach we’ve taken,” he said.

“Since we won the first match, an even bigger challenge awaits us. (But) winning a Test match is never easy. Right now, we just want to carry this momentum forward, and we’ll plan for the next match later.”

The victory came on the back of a disappointing thrashing to Cricket Australia XI just prior to the first Test when they were bowled out for just 54 in their second innings of Bangladesh’s only tour match, but Miraz said the side’s management never lost faith in their ability.

title: Lanka Rowing League begins bold new chapter for Sri Lankan rowing | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 18 August 2026 10:32
-     - 1

From left: Akthab Cader, Michael Sathasivam, Hardy Jamaldeen, Gamindu Tennakoon, Minsandee Kalutotage, and Nilanka Pieris

Sri Lankan sport entered a new era with the official launch of the Lanka Rowing League, the country’s first-ever franchise-based rowing competition. Unveiled at a press conference at the Colombo Rowing Club, the new league will transform one of the country’s most historic sports into a fast-paced, city-based championship built around elite competition, team identity and passionate rivalry.

The inaugural Lanka Rowing League will feature six franchises representing Kandy, Sigiriya, Mirissa, Trinco, Galle and Colombo. On 19 and 20 December 2026, these teams will compete through a Group Stage and Semi-Finals before racing for the honour of becoming Sri Lanka’s first franchise rowing champions.

The competition will feature the Men’s Single Sculls (1x), Men’s Pair (2-), Women’s Double Sculls (2x) and Men’s Coxed Four (4+), bringing individual skill, team precision and high-stakes racing together in one championship.

The Lanka Rowing League is owned by Elevate Sports, led by co-owners Viren Beruwalage and Anuk Suraweera. Suraweera is a former oarsman who brings first-hand knowledge of the sport, while Colombo Aces Principal owner Beruwalage brings valuable franchise ownership experience. Together, they aim to build a league that respects the traditions of rowing while presenting the sport in a bold and accessible new format.

From left: Eventsitry Sports Co-Founder Ifham Arrif, Elevate Sports Lanka Co-Founders Viren Beruwalage and Anuk Suraweera, and Eventsitry Sports Co-Founder Karin Wijeratne

“This is more than the launch of a new league—it is a chance to redefine how Sri Lanka sees and experiences rowing,” said Beruwalage and Suraweera. “For the first time, cities will have teams to call their own, athletes will race with a new sense of identity and supporters will have rivalries to follow. We are taking rowing beyond the water and turning it into a national sporting spectacle.”

Elevate Sports will deliver the league in partnership with Eventistry Sports, a leader in Sri Lanka’s franchise-sports sector. Eventistry Sports owns the Sri Lanka Padel League, Ceylon Pickle League and Lanka Tennis League and manages and operates the Ceylon Golf League and The Next XV Franchise Rugby League. Its proven experience in developing franchise competitions, combined with the rowing and ownership knowledge within Elevate Sports, provides the Lanka Rowing League with a strong foundation for long-term growth.

The Kandy franchise is owned by Michael Sathasivam and Rajitha Siriwardana; Sigiriya by Akthab Cader and Ruvendran Weerasinghe; Mirissa by Gamindu Tennakoon, Sajaad Ajmal and Vimodha Abeywardene; Trinco by Hardy Jamaldeen and Shafras Rilwan; Galle by Imal Kalutotage, Minsandee Kalutotage and Seyara Alwis; and Colombo by Nilanka Pieris and Oceanie De Silva.

With six cities, four boat classes and one historic championship at stake, the Lanka Rowing League will place Sri Lankan rowing on a new national stage. Further announcements regarding the teams, athletes and inaugural championship will be made ahead of the opening races in December.

title: DFCC Bank Cricket Sixes: Beyond the boundary, building lifelong friendships | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 18 August 2026 10:30
-     - 1

There are days at DFCC Bank when conversations revolve around liquidity, customer experience, digital innovation, and sustainable growth. Then there are days when the most hotly debated issue is whether that ball really carried to slip.

The DFCC Bank Staff Cricket Sixes 2026 was one of those days.

From the moment the opening parade entered the grounds of D.S. Senanayake College, it was clear this was no ordinary staff sporting event. Twenty-four teams from across the Bank arrived in full colour, carrying names such as the Jaffna Strikers, Eastern Phoenix, Credit Hub Knights, HO Sharks, Southern Warriors, and Central Lions.

Following the opening ceremony, the National Anthem and Bank Song echoed across the grounds. Then cricket took over.

There were elegant cover drives, towering sixes, sharp catches, clever bowling changes, and determined partnerships. There were also deliveries that appeared to ignore the laws of physics, ambitious running between the wickets, and catches that seemed to disagree with gravity. Fortunately, nobody allowed technique to stand in the way of enthusiasm.

The diversity of the tournament was one of its strongest features. Colleagues travelled from across the island, many leaving home before dawn to represent their branch or department. For some, it was the first opportunity to meet teammates previously known through emails, Teams calls, or phone conversations. Before long, introductions had turned into partnerships, rivalries, and friendships.

The requirement for every team to include a female player added further energy. Women confidently took the field, claimed wickets, found boundaries, and proved that good cricket has never depended on job title, geography, or gender.

A major highlight was the exhibition match between the Corporate Management Team and the Senior Management Team. Strong performances kept spectators along the boundary before Deputy CEO Shamindra Marcelline’s final-ball six settled the contest and created a friendly rivalry likely to continue next year.

Yet the real story unfolded between deliveries: in applause for the opposition, encouragement for first-time players, and laughter after every dropped catch or ambitious appeal. The values that define DFCC Bank’s culture, passion, authenticity, courage, collaboration, and excellence—were visible throughout the day.

The tournament was made possible through the dedicated efforts of the DFCC Welfare Association, whose coordination ensured the event ran smoothly.

When the final wicket fell, Ramanayake Charges emerged as champions, while the Credit Hub Knights finished as worthy runners-up.

The trophies and medals will be remembered, but perhaps the tournament’s greatest legacy is the reminder that the strongest partnerships are not always built in meeting rooms. Sometimes, they begin with a shared laugh, a hard-earned run, or a six that travelled further than anyone expected.

title: Asia Rugby Sevens takes centre stage in China and Sri Lanka | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 18 August 2026 10:19
-     - 3

By Shamseer Jaleel

The 2026 Asia Rugby Emirates Sevens Series will take on added significance this year as the region’s leading teams battle not only for honours but also for valuable exposure and a pathway towards the next level of international sevens rugby.

The series will open in Suzhou, China, on 29 August before moving to Colombo for the second and final round on 17 and 18 October. With both the men’s and women’s competitions featuring 12 nations, the two tournaments will provide an important platform for established sides while also highlighting the rapid progress of emerging rugby nations across Asia.

The significance of the competition extends beyond the two rounds. Strong performances in the Asian sevens pathway will be crucial for teams targeting higher international recognition, including opportunities to qualify for the 50-year-old, world-famous Hong Kong Sevens and, ultimately, the World Rugby Sevens pathway.

The inclusion of emerging nations such as Iran, Uzbekistan, India and Kazakhstan is particularly encouraging. Their progress through development competitions such as the Emirates Sevens Trophy demonstrates that investment in structured pathways is producing tangible results and expanding the competitive base of Asian rugby.

For Sri Lanka, the Colombo round will be especially important. Playing at home provides the national teams with an opportunity to perform in front of local supporters while testing themselves against some of the strongest sevens programs in Asia.

The men’s competition includes Hong Kong China, Japan, Sri Lanka, China, the United Arab Emirates, Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, Korea, Kazakhstan, India and Uzbekistan.

The women’s series features Japan, China, Thailand, Hong Kong China, Kazakhstan, India, Singapore, the UAE, Malaysia, Sri Lanka, Uzbekistan and Iran.

The pathway towards Hong Kong is particularly significant. The Hong Kong Sevens remains one of the most prestigious events in the Asian and global rugby calendar and an important stepping stone towards the global sevens arena. Success in the Asian circuit can therefore provide nations with the confidence and competitive experience required to pursue bigger international objectives, including the World Rugby Sevens pathway.

With Suzhou launching the campaign and Colombo bringing the series to a close, the 2026 Asia Rugby Emirates Sevens Series promises to be more than a two-round tournament. It will be a key stage in Asia’s continuing development and a potential launch-pad for nations chasing Hong Kong qualification and a place closer to the global World Series pathway in 2027.

Former Isipathana and Kandy SC player Srinath Sooriyabandara will lead the outfit, which will be coached by Peter Woods. The rest of the squad will be named tomorrow (19).

title: Sri Lanka not out of the woods yet despite Dinusha-Dickwella defiance | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 18 August 2026 10:19
-     - 2

By Sa’adi Thawfeeq reporting from Galle

GALLE: Sonal Dinusha’s maiden Test hundred and Niroshan Dickwella’s 23rd Test fifty stood out in Sri Lanka’s first innings of 284 on the third day of the first cricket Test against India at the Galle International Cricket Stadium yesterday.

Dinusha and Dickwella were involved in a determined partnership of 146 for the sixth wicket that not only frustrated the Indian bowling but also ensured they crossed the follow-on deficit and made India bat again.

With dark clouds and bad light preventing India from commencing their second innings, the day ended with Sri Lanka still on the back foot as they trailed by 178 runs with two days left in the match. Their only hope is for further interruptions from the weather in the remaining days.

India would have been slightly disappointed to let Sri Lanka recover from 59-4 to their final total. Dickwella rode his luck and played a breezy knock of 80 off 115 balls (7 fours) missing out on a maiden Test hundred for the 98th time. He holds the record for the most fifty-plus scores without a hundred in Tests with 23. The next highest is 16 by India’s Chetan Chauhan.  

Dinusha showed outstanding composure to play a very mature knock of 100 off 168 balls (4 fours, 2 sixes). The pair denied India a single wicket in the afternoon session as Sri Lanka managed 116 runs off 29 overs scoring at four runs per over. Sri Lanka were in all sorts of trouble in the first session losing five wickets for 99 with the threat of giving India a chance of enforcing the follow-on. But Dinusha and Dickwella threw that thought out of the window with their face-saving stand.

India didn’t declare overnight but the final pair lasted just four deliveries in the morning when play resumed on time. Prasidh Krishna was bounced out by Asitha Fernando edging a catch behind the wicket and India got bowled out for 462.

Mohamed Siraj provided the early breakthrough for India with his second ball as he nipped out Nishan Madushka with a gentle outswinger which the batsman gave catching practice to the slips cordon. Lahiru Udara hit a few boundaries but Dinesh Chandimal never looked comfortable at the crease. He was dismissed by Manav Suthar, who struck with his very first ball.

Udara got a start but failed to convert it into anything substantial. After getting beaten by a sharp turning ball, he was dismissed slicing a cut to backward point. Sri Lanka lost two more wickets in the session with Shubman Gill taking a brilliant catch to dismiss Kamindu Mendis and Dhananjaya de Silva knicking Ravindra Jadeja to slip for Sri Lanka to go to lunch tottering at 99-5. Suthar and Kuldeep Yadav got three of the top four after Siraj’s opening burst.

Following a wicketless second session Indian bowlers came back to capture the remaining five Sri Lankan wickets with Suthar landing the final blow in an innings where he only enhanced his reputation. Playing just his second Test, he was arguably the pick of the bowlers finishing with 4/76 off 21.4 overs, alongside veteran Jadeja (3/57).

title: Australia greats want change as Cummins ponders way forward | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 18 August 2026 10:17
-     - 2

Australia Captain Pat Cummins

Australia great and former national selector Mark Waugh has put the onus on the Aussies’ top-order following their shock nine-wicket loss to Bangladesh in Darwin.

The ICC World Test Championship pacesetters fell to their second loss of the current cycle when humbled by Bangladesh at Marrara Stadium and have little time to lick their wounds ahead of the second and final Test of the series in Mackay that commences on Saturday.

Only two members of Australia’s 13-player squad - Josh Inglis and Scott Boland - missed selection for that first Test in Darwin, though the Aussies have the option of calling on other players from outside the squad should they wish to make changes for the second Test.

Waugh, a former national selector and an Australian batting legend that scored 20 Test centuries during his international career, suggested something was amiss in the Aussies’ top-order and newcomer Jake Weatherald and veteran No.3 Marnus Labuschagne were the players under the most pressure to hold their spot going forward.

 “It’s really about the batting and the top three,” Waugh told Fox Cricket.

 “OK, we’ll leave Travis Head (opening) there for the moment. I don’t think he’s an opener, but anyway, he’s going to open.

 “It’s Jake Weatherald and Marnus Labuschagne. Those guys need runs. There’s no doubt about it.

 “I’m just wondering whether the selectors have said them to before this Test: ‘OK, you’ve got these two Test matches to prove your spot in the team’.

 “I’m concerned about Jake Weatherald. Looking at him, he’s trying to tinker with his technique. I think there’s lot of things going on in his head.

 “He hasn’t made big runs for a while. He’s got runs in the bank, which is sort of keeping him in the side.

 “I think it’s a 50/50 call on these guys for the next Test. I think Weatherald’s probably the one in the biggest danger. Marnus, I’d give him another go.”

If Australia do decide to make changes to their batting group for the second Test against Bangladesh then Inglis is the most likely option given he is already in the squad, while the likes of Matthew Renshaw, Ollie Peake or Nathan McSweeney are other batters that could come into contention.

Former Australia opener Matthew Hayden suggested a left-field approach, with the ICC Hall of Famer believing Head could find his best form with a move to No.3 and that the Aussies should look at including two new openers for the second Test.

Australia Captain Pat Cummins was quizzed about the likelihood of changes following the shock loss in the first Test and the Test skipper said selectors would require 24-48 hours before they make any decision.

“I think it’s a balance of ‘It’s one Test’ – but it’s also a little bit of a trend as well,” he said. 

“So it’s trying to work out, do you need to intervene now, or do you let it play out and think (the current group) is the way forward?

title: Playing with Dickwella gave me confidence – Dinusha | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 18 August 2026 10:17
-     - 2

Sonal Dinusha who scored his maiden Test century and helped Sri Lanka avert the follow-on against India in the first Test at Galle said that he gained confidence while batting with Niroshan Dickwella.

The pair put on a partnership of 146 for the sixth wicket after Sri Lanka had lost half the side for 99 at lunch and saw them post a final total of 284 in reply to India’s 462.      

“Even though we were five wickets down we spoke about hitting every ball we could,” said Dinusha at the end of the day.

“It was the first time I played with Dickwella. He played his usual style of play and that gave me confidence. It was great for him to get that kind of score under pressure.”

Dickwella, returning to Test cricket after a lapse of three years went onto score 80, once again missing out on an opportunity to make a maiden Test hundred, and Dinusha made exactly 100.

Sweeps and reverse sweeps kept the Indian bowlers at bay during the partnership and playing against three left-arm spinners also helped in some way, said Dinusha.

“There was a slight advantage there, but they didn’t let us hit easily. Playing in Galle with the ball spinning is something we should expect. Sweeping and playing off the back foot are also important in this circumstance.”

Dinusha said that he had small plans during his innings. “What I did for the most part was to focus more and play to my strengths. I have batted at number 6 or 7 throughout my career and I hope to continue playing as a middle-order batsman.”

Left-arm spinner Manav Suthar who was India’s successful spinner with 4/76 said that he was happy he got a wicket off the first ball.

“Dinesh Chandimal is their most experienced batter so pretty pleased with that. There was a lot of assistance for the spin bowlers, but it was important that we put the ball in the right areas and created opportunities. I thought all the bowlers did a decent job to get ourselves ahead of the game.” [ST]

Army SC and Galle CC maintained their undefeated record in Group B of the Tier B 50-over tournament registering their third consecutive win yesterday.

Army SC ended Chilaw Marians CC’s successful runs with a 23-run win (DLS method) at Surrey grounds, Maggona. Chilaw Marians CC were all out for 154 in 32.3 overs with skipper Kasun Vidura making a top score of 68 off 65 balls (9 fours, 1 six). Army SC replied with 122-4 in 24 overs when bad light ended the match. At that point Army SC were ahead on the DLS run rate.

Galle CC also won on the DLS method beating Kandy Customs SC by 48 runs at the Mahinda Rajapaksa Stadium, Hambantota. Galle CC rattled off 261-9 with Yuthika de Silva scoring 81 off 75 balls (8 fours, 2 sixes) and skipper Amith Eranda 41 off 44. Kandy Customs SC chasing a revised target of 256 in 47 overs managed only 207-9 with Eranda shining with the ball taking 3/41. Kaveesha Induwara top scored with 53* off 57 balls (5 fours, 1 six).

Kurunegala SC pulled off a thrilling four-run win against Negombo CC at Air Force grounds, Katunayake. Negombo CC chasing 256 for victory managed 251-8 despite Dinitha Lochana scoring 79 off 99 balls (7 fours, 2 sixes). Half-centuries from Dilshan Kollure (69 off 82 balls, 2 fours, 2 sixes) and Rajitha Rathnayake (61 off 91 balls, 6 fours) saw Kurunegala SC reach 255. Right-arm seamer Hansaja Hiruna took 6/47.

In the other matches completed Southern teams Moratuwa SC and Sebastianites both won their respective matches. Moratuwa SC beat Navy SC by four wickets (DLS method) at De Soysa Stadium, Moratuwa. Navy SC’s innings ended at 129-9 in 35.3 overs with rain curtailing play. Moratuwa SC chasing a revised target of 96 replied with 98-6.

Sebastianites edged out United Southern CC by seven runs (DLS method) at SLLDC, Kirimandala. Eranga Jayakody’s knock of 74* off 120 balls (5 fours) enabled Sebastianites total 184-8. United Southern SC chasing a revised target of 147 in 31 overs finished on 139-9. Former Jaffna Hindu College captain Sutharsan Subarnan took 4/11 with spin and Punsara Sandaruwan 3/23 with pace.
